title: Smart energy must address enshittification risks - Nature Energy
gist: A commentary arguing that as heat pumps, EVs and other connected devices become the delivery layer for energy services, the platform owners coordinating them will acquire the same lock-in and market power that produced 'enshittification' in social networks. It frames digitalized energy as a platform-economics problem — switching costs, network effects and natural monopoly — rather than purely an engineering one.

themes.theme: Enshittification thesis applied to energy platforms

insights.claim: The 'enshittification' pattern — platform owners pivoting from attracting customers to exploiting accumulated market power, with service quality declining as a result — is argued to be a live risk in the energy sector, not just in social networking.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Assume connected-energy platforms will eventually monetise captive users; that raises terminal margins but also the odds of regulatory intervention.
insights.quote: the term describes the shift by platform owners from attracting customers to exploiting market power, leading to worse services
insights.locator: Second paragraph: 'Coined by Doctorow, the term describes...'

insights.claim: The concept being applied to energy was coined by Cory Doctorow, who has separately written that cleantech specifically has an enshittification problem tied to unplanned obsolescence of connected hardware.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: The critique now has a mainstream vocabulary and a peer-reviewed venue, which is usually a leading indicator of consumer-protection rulemaking.
insights.locator: References: 'Doctorow, C. Cleantech has an enshittification problem'

insights.claim: The central open question posed is whether digitalization of the energy transition itself introduces new forms of market power and consumer vulnerability, treating digitalization as a source of risk rather than only an efficiency gain.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Counterweight to the default bullish framing of grid digitalization; the same data that enables flexibility creates the lock-in.
insights.quote: could digitalization introduce new forms of market power and consumer vulnerability?
insights.locator: First paragraph: 'This raises a question for the energy transition'

themes.theme: Device layer as the control point

insights.claim: Energy services are increasingly delivered through digitally connected devices such as heat pumps and electric vehicles, which makes the device and its software the actual customer interface rather than the utility tariff.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Value migrates from the commodity electron to whoever owns the device firmware and the app — watch OEM software stacks, not just kWh margins.
insights.quote: the energy services we use are delivered through digitally connected devices such as heat pumps and electric vehicles (EVs)
insights.locator: Opening: 'Increasingly, the energy services we use are delivered...'

insights.claim: Consumers are expected to become progressively less able to opt out of connected energy ecosystems, which is the precondition that converts a convenience product into a captive one.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Falling opt-out rates are what underwrite recurring-revenue models in home energy; they are also the trigger for switching-cost regulation.
insights.quote: consumers may become less able to opt out of these connected ecosystems
insights.locator: Opening paragraph: 'At the same time, consumers may become less able to opt out'

insights.claim: As energy systems electrify and decentralize, system stability is said to depend on ever more sophisticated coordination of distributed devices, meaning the coordination layer becomes infrastructure the grid cannot do without.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Whoever operates that coordination layer holds a quasi-essential-facility position — high moat, high regulatory target.
insights.quote: their stability will depend on ever more sophisticated coordination of distributed devices
insights.locator: Opening paragraph: 'As energy systems electrify and decentralize'

insights.claim: The argument is anchored in classical industrial-organization literature on switching costs, network effects and two-sided markets rather than in energy engineering, implying the failure mode is economic structure and not technology maturity.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Use platform-market analytical tools to value and stress-test smart-energy businesses; the moat and the antitrust exposure are the same asset.
insights.locator: References: Klemperer, The New Palgrave Dictionary of Economics; Katz, M. L. & Shapiro, C.

insights.claim: Network effects are explicitly extended from traditional grid connections to smart grids in the cited work, suggesting smart-grid participation gets more valuable as more devices join and therefore tips toward concentration.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Expect winner-take-most dynamics in home-energy aggregation platforms; early installed-base share is the metric that compounds.
insights.locator: References: 'Network effects from electricity grid connections: from traditional grids to smart grids'

insights.claim: The commentary draws on work treating digital platform markets as natural monopolies, which is the analytical basis on which structural remedies rather than conduct fines are usually justified.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: If regulators adopt the natural-monopoly framing for energy platforms, interoperability mandates or price controls become plausible tail risks.
insights.locator: References: 'Ducci, F. in Natural Monopolies in Digital Platform Markets'

insights.claim: Right-to-repair and computer-law scholarship is cited alongside the market-power literature, connecting connected-device obsolescence and repair restrictions to the same enshittification dynamic in energy hardware.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Repair and firmware-support obligations would compress the aftermarket and forced-replacement revenue built into connected heat pump and EV charging models.
insights.locator: References: 'Boniface, C., Urquhart, L. & Terras, M. Comput. Law Secur. Rev.'

insights.claim: The piece is publicly funded research from UCL's Institute for Sustainable Resources and Energy Institute under a UKRI award, indicating UK academic and funder attention is being directed at smart-energy consumer harms ahead of any market failure.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: UK policy discourse on smart-energy consumer protection is forming now; UK-exposed flexibility and heat-pump platforms should price in early rules.
insights.locator: Acknowledgements and Author information: 'M.F. received funding for this article from UKRI'
